sections.content: Soler + infinitive describes actions that happen regularly or habitually. It is especially useful when talking about routines and health habits. Habitual meaning can also be expressed with the present tense, expressions such as *normalmente* and cada día, or frequency phrases.

items.spanish: Suelo caminar después de cenar porque me ayuda a dormir.
items.english: I usually walk after dinner because it helps me sleep.

items.spanish: Los fines de semana solemos cocinar en casa.
items.english: At weekends we usually cook at home.

items.spanish: Normalmente duermo siete horas, aunque durante los viajes duermo menos.
items.english: I normally sleep seven hours, although during trips I sleep less.

items.spanish: Evito los hábitos que pueden resultar perjudiciales para mi salud.
items.english: I avoid habits that can be harmful to my health.

sections.content: Soler is followed by an infinitive. The form changes according to the subject: *suelo*, sueles, suele, *solemos*, suelen.
